coachingPoints: Reduce decisions in drills before adding them in games — 2v1 before 3v2, 3v2 before 5v5.
Praise quick, correct decisions more loudly than made shots.
Use constraints: "you have three seconds to shoot, drive, or pass."
Teach the decision tree, not just the outcome — players should know why the choice was right.
commonMistakes: Predetermining the move before reading what the defense shows.
Holding the ball too long while waiting for the "perfect" option.
Forcing a bad shot instead of making the simple, available pass.
Second-guessing mid-move — the in-between game of half-drives and aborted fakes.
description: A simple framework for making faster, better decisions on the court — read, decide, execute — under real game pressure.
gameSituations: 2-on-1 fast break: read the lone defender's commitment to choose pass or finish.
Catch against a closeout: shoot it, drive it, or swing it — decided on the catch.
Late shot clock: simplify to your best one or two options and commit.

howTo.detail: On every catch ask in order: can I shoot? If no, can I drive? If no, move the ball. Three questions, always in the same order, answered in under two seconds.
howTo.title: Simplify to three options

howTo.detail: Make your read while the ball is in the air so you act the instant it arrives. Deciding on the catch keeps you ahead of the rotating defense.
howTo.title: Decide on the catch

howTo.detail: If they go under the screen, shoot. If they help off your man, pass to him. Do not fight the defense — accept what it gives you and punish it.
howTo.title: Take what the defense gives

howTo.detail: If you have not decided within two seconds of catching the ball, pass it and relocate. Holding the ball kills advantages and lets the defense recover.
howTo.title: Use the two-second rule

howTo.detail: Once you drive, drive. Once you shoot, shoot. Hesitation in the middle of a decision creates the turnovers that confident mistakes never do.
howTo.title: Commit to the choice

howTo.detail: Analyze decisions after the game with film, not during the possession. In the game, trust your preparation; after it, sharpen your reads.
howTo.title: Review after, not during

title: Decision Making
whatIsIt: Decision making is the process of choosing what to do — shoot, drive, or pass — in the half-second you have the ball. Every possession is a chain of small decisions, and the best players are not the ones who make perfect choices; they are the ones who make good choices quickly.

Good decisions come from a repeatable process: read the defense, pick the best available option, and commit fully. Indecision — the half-drive, the pump-fake into nothing — is worse than a wrong decision made with confidence.
whyItMatters: Games are decided by possessions, and possessions are decided by decisions. A team that consistently makes the simple, correct read will beat a more athletic team that guesses. Coaches build offenses to create decisions; players who decide well make any offense work.

Decision speed also compounds. One quick, correct decision forces the defense to rotate; the next quick decision attacks that rotation. Slow decisions let the defense rest, and rested defenses do not break.
